title: Transaction
description: The normalised transaction that every bankhub source emits and every destination consumes -- the interlingua of the hub. This schema describes the JSON form (the Python dataclass's to_dict()): Decimals are strings, dates are ISO-8601. Amount is SIGNED: negative = money out (debit/outflow), positive = money in (credit/inflow).

external_id.description: Stable, deterministic id used to de-duplicate across runs. Use the source's own immutable id when it has one; otherwise compute one (see SPEC.md 'Identity & de-duplication').

source.description: Name of the producing source, optionally namespaced, e.g. 'csv:revolut' or 'plaid'.

account_id.description: Source-side account identifier (account number, currency, Plaid account_id, ...).

amount.description: Signed decimal serialised as a string (never a float, to avoid binary rounding error). Negative = outflow, positive = inflow.

posted_date.description: Date the transaction posted, if distinct from 'date'.

balance.description: Running account balance after this transaction, if the source provides it (signed decimal string).

raw.description: The original source record, retained for debugging and re-processing. Opaque to the engine.
